description: Hidden Phase-1 case used Phase-2 syntax (BETWEEN); conforming Phase-1 engines answer UNSUPPORTED.
impact: Validation verdict only (hidden test); runs re-validated, earlier verdict kept in validation-history/.
prevention: spec_validate lints Phase-1 cases for Phase-2 syntax.

description: Runner overwrote explicit ids of request steps with its step counter, so the two id-echo cases in phase1/limits_and_output.pqt failed for every engine.
impact: Agents saw 2 spurious public failures during development (possible wasted effort; inspect transcripts before attributing effort metrics). Validation verdicts re-computed.

description: Validation used the workspace copy of tests/ and spec/, which an agent could modify.
impact: None observed: no workspace modified tests/, spec/, datasets/ or tools/ (verified with git diff against the baseline commit).

description: Java and Go agents independently noted that comparing an INT64 beyond 18 digits with a DECIMAL raises NUMERIC_OVERFLOW under the literal promotion rule. Candidate clarification via change control after the wave.

Fuzzer required an error for 'SELECT 1+1+...+1' (20001 terms), which is valid SQL with no spec size limit (correct answer 20001). Go, Java, Clojure and Common Lisp were correct and were reported as 1 problem each.
impact: Robustness results only (fuzz is not part of acceptance). Fixed: such inputs must yield the correct result or a clean non-INTERNAL error; setup load is asserted; succeeded responses are counted.

description: The spec has no implementation limits for expression size/nesting. Rust answers a 20001-term expression with PARSE_ERROR (others compute it). Candidate change: allow RESOURCE_LIMIT for exceeding documented implementation limits, require a minimum supported depth (e.g. 1000).
impact: no agent run affected (not visible to agents); engines built against spec 1.0.0 are measured against CR-6 for information only
resolution: Resolved 2026-10-12 by change request CR-6 (spec/changes/expression-limits.md, ADR-0017, capability change.expression_limits). The robustness probes also found crashes and timeouts that are not enforced on such statements (results/correctness/robustness/)

description: Hand-written CR-1 case (line 51, not oracle-checked) expected DECIMAL(18,2) for INT64 UNION ALL orders.amount, but the case loaded orders.csv without a schema; inference never yields DECIMAL, so amount is FLOAT64 and FLOAT64 is the correct answer. Go, Python and Rust all returned FLOAT64 and were classified tests_failed.
impact: Spurious public failure visible to every change-union-all agent; affected runs re-validated with the fixed case, earlier verdicts kept in validation-history/.
prevention: Hand-written expectations get an explicit schema for DECIMAL columns; run new change cases against at least one engine (expected failures only on the new capability) before launching a wave.

description: Run time limits were capped by the OAuth token's remaining lifetime at launch, so chained optimize-latency runs got 72-104 min limits depending on launch time (requested 330). Go, Python and Java were killed by the limit (exit 124) and, because classify() checked validation before the exit code, were reported as success although the agents had not finished.
impact: Three runs re-classified as timeout (committed work still validates; not merged). Rust and Clojure (limits 104/100 min) finished voluntarily after 44/41 min and are unaffected. The family is re-run with a uniform 120-min limit: Go/Python/Java attempt 2, Common Lisp attempt 1 (not yet started when found).
prevention: Runs wait for a token covering the requested limit (max(75, min(limit+15, 160)) min); exit 124/137 is classified as timeout before validation; termination_reason records timeouts.

description: The optimize-latency task told agents to optimize `benchmarks/workloads/analytics.json` at scale 1m, but `benchmarks/` was not among the paths exported into agent workspaces, so the file never existed for any optimize-latency run. Every agent wrote its own stand-in workload (Clojure 30 queries, Java 25, others similar) and optimized and measured against that instead.
impact: The optimization target differed per language (self-written workloads with different query mixes), so the agents' own speedup numbers are not comparable and the independent before/after on the real workload (results/performance/optimize-latency-before-after.json) measures transfer from each agent's stand-in to the official workload, not optimization of the official workload. Correctness results are unaffected. Found while answering a user question about the Clojure optimizations.
prevention: TASK_EXTRA_PATHS exports benchmarks/workloads for optimize-latency; a re-run of the family (attempt n+1) on the real workload is needed for a like-for-like optimization comparison.

description: Engine validation for the later task families overlays the trusted native-kernels/reference-c, Makefile and tests onto the agent's clone, but not native-kernels/include. After the CR-4 merge the trusted reference-c used pqk_i128 while the clone's header (from the run's base ref, before CR-4) did not define it, so `make -C native-kernels all` failed (native_lib_exit=2). The classifier ignored native_lib_exit, and engines may silently fall back to their own code when the library cannot be loaded (phase-5.md), so the --native conformance run passed without any native kernels.
impact: Only validation of these six record-only runs (the first engine validations after CR-4). Their native conformance verdicts were vacuous; all other checks were valid. No outcome flipped to success because of it (Python was tests_failed for the HTTP suite anyway). Found while checking the Python failure.
prevention: native-kernels/include joins the trusted overlay; the native conformance step records native_exit=3 when the library is missing; classify() fails closed on nonzero native_lib_exit/native_exit. The six runs were re-validated (previous verdicts kept in validation-history/).

description: The before/after script created both worktrees at HEAD and then ran `git checkout <ref> -- implementations/<lang>`, which adds and updates files but does not delete files that exist at HEAD and not at the ref. The measured 'before' (and in round 2 also 'after') trees therefore contained 2-9 extra files per engine (unreferenced source files added or removed by optimization runs, and the agents' own benchmark scripts). Found when the Track B Java 'before' build failed on such a file.
affected_results: results/performance/optimize-latency-before-after.json (round 1: rust, clojure, java, python, common-lisp before)
results/performance/optimize-latency-before-after-a2.json (round 2: all but go, before and after)
impact: Likely none on timings: the stray files were not referenced by the builds (Rust/Common Lisp compile declared modules only, Clojure AOT-compiles what main requires, Python imports what is referenced; Java compiled the extra classes but nothing used them); Go was unaffected. Correctness results are unaffected (validation clones the workspace). All three before/after sets (both optimize rounds and Track B jvm-tuning) were re-measured with the fixed script; the earlier figures remain in git history.
prevention: before_after.sh deletes the engine directory before the checkout and aborts unless each measured tree is identical to its ref (no differing or untracked files).

description: The cross-engine result digest hashed the JSON form of each value after rounding floats to 6 decimals, so a FLOAT64 written as an integral JSON number (79) and as 79.0 hashed differently, although the spec allows both (spec/data-types/types.md, FLOAT64 encoding). At 10m rows q16_timeseries_hourly has MAX(humidity) = 79.0 in one group; both assembly engines write it as 79, so the 10m benchmark reported two distinct q16 results.
impact: No engine was wrong. A sandboxed re-run of q16 on the six x86 engines (results/performance/20261013T111035Z-10m-main-and-asm-x86/q16-digest-recheck.json) reproduces the recorded digests with the old rule and gives one digest for all engines with the fixed rule; the AArch64 engine recorded the same pre-fix digest as the x86-64 engine. Earlier benchmarks (1m and below) had full agreement and are unaffected. Timings are unaffected.
prevention: digest() uses the response's column types: integral JSON numbers in FLOAT64 columns are converted to float before rounding and hashing.

description: The large-data probe generated the 10m dataset with pqgen --jobs 8. Inside the validation sandbox Python multiprocessing cannot create POSIX semaphores (no writable /dev/shm), so generation failed with PermissionError and the probe exited before starting the engine; the first validation of a-fix-large-data-common-lisp-a1 was classified tests_failed with large_data_exit=1 although the engine was never exercised.
impact: One wrong verdict; the run was re-validated with the fixed probe (success, all four large-data checks pass); the earlier verdict is kept in validation-history/.
prevention: The probe retries generation single-process when parallel generation fails.

description: The storage benchmark saved transactions (with its two workload indexes) and reopened the file under new table names while the live table still held the indexes. Index names are catalog-global (protocol.md §5.7), so every engine correctly answered open with ALREADY_EXISTS; all open_* entries in every earlier benchmark have ok=false and their open_seconds time a rejected request.
impact: Cold/warm open times in all benchmark summaries before 9edc603 are invalid (save times and file sizes are valid). No results document quotes open times; no engine verdict depended on them.
prevention: The harness drops the live table's indexes after the save, and records the error code of a failed open.

description: The run guard treated the rate-limit status allowed_warning (seven-day utilization crossed 0.75) as a stop condition and stopped all six app-pqledger agents at 17:24 UTC; the two assembly chains started session 2, which was stopped within seconds. Java, Clojure and both assembly runs had passing apps but no APP.md/EMBEDDING.md yet (docs_exit 1). Costs of the stopped sessions were not reported by the agent CLI (null).
fix: Maintainer instruction: weekly start threshold raised to 0.98; allowed_warning is no longer a stop condition, the guard stops at seven_day >= 0.98 (PQ_MAX_7D_UTIL_RUN), five_hour >= 0.95, any other non-allowed status or overage. The four runs resume as continuation sessions.

description: The C-compilation check matched the text of every tool input, including file content: a Write of the AArch64 EMBEDDING.md, whose C-ABI section shows how a C program links libpolyquery (gcc ... prog.c), was reported as a C compilation (false positive, a-app-pqledger-arm64-asm-engine-a1-s2-20261014T181408Z). No C file was written or compiled.
fix: The compile pattern is applied to executed shell commands only; a new check, high_level_files_written, flags any Write/Edit of a high-level source path anywhere (except the declarations-only include/polyquery.h). Verified on synthetic violations; all earlier assembly runs still pass.
